cards.note: KM markers that start with PE are national roads. If they have 2 different letters they are regional and those letters are an abbreviation for the region name. They will also have a different color than black.
Poles in Peru occasionally have the region name (or an abbreviation for it) written on them.
Pole marking starting with an A followed by 4 digits are only found in Tumbes and Piura regions.
6 digits vertical pole markings are common in Tumbes and Piura (can also be found in Lambayeque, Cajamarca and Tacna).

7 digits vertical pole markings are common in Cajamarca, La Libertad and Ancash (rarely Piura, Lambayeque, Tacna). The code can start with 0 or another digit. If it's not 0 it tells you the region: 2 & 4 - Ancash; 3 - Cajamarca; 5 - La Libertad
Only found in Piura region (very common in Sullana). Usually you won’t be able to see all the 8 digits (0000-0000). In Sullana sometimes you can find it with only 7 digits (000-0000)
8 digits vertical pole markings are found in La Libertad region (rarely Cajamarca, Ancash)
9 digits vertical pole markings are rare but can be found in Lambayeque (sometimes Ancash). Sometimes there are two letters instead of the first two digits.
Red on white / blue on white digits vertical are common in Arequipa region. Rarely the red on white markings can be found in Lima.

These stickers are mainly in the regions of Tumbes, Piura, Ica and Lima. Differences: Lima - Big numbers in the middle; Ica - Readable numbers at the bottom; Piura & Tumbes: Very small numbers at the bottom.
This is the most common style of the warning stickers in the northern half of the country.
In Callao you often find a light blue - dark blue painted section at the bottom of the poles.
Most of the COMOL poles are found in Arequipa region (rarely in Cusco).

Very long horizontal Pole markings. Common in Junin, Pasco and Huanuco (sometimes Ayacucho, Huancavelica). Typically, the shorter code starts with a 4. The next two letters refer to the region you are in.
Definitely most common in Piura but Tumbes also has them.
Can be either in the form of a sticker: blue text on white background with black border or in a form of regular marking similar to company name markings. Useful for getting Lambayeque.

3 Letters and 3 Digits horizontal pole markings. The letters are an abbreviation for nearby towns (scannable!). Can also be 2 letters, 4 digits. Useful to memorize: CJ - Cajamarca; HI - Trujillo; EN - Chiclayo; CH - Chimbote
ICASAC are in Ica (rarely Ayacucho) region. HHSAC are in Ica (rarely Huancavelica) region.
LDS poles are unique to Lima region.
In the city of Pucallpa you can often find poles with this combination of these four stickers.
These rotated numbers markings are only found in Apurimac, Cusco and Madre de Dios. In Cusco, you can sometimes find it with other rotated markings.
Poles with support can be found in the south, most common in Puno, Cusco and Apurimac. Poles without support can be found in the north, most common in Cajamarca.
These blue on white divided markings are only in Tacna and Moquegua regions. Colors can sometimes be inverted as white on blue.
White kV stickers can be found in Lambayeque, Cajamarca (rarely Amazonas) regions. The letters on these stickers may refer to the nearby city’s name. For example: JAE - Jaén.
These yellow warning stickers which contain information about voltage (kV) are unique to Ica region and very common.
